name: int_repr
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::int_repr(Tensor self) -> Tensor. Other registered schemas, copied verbatim: aten::int_repr.out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!) . This definition describes only the representative overload; the original Gems pytest owns the complete contract for every overload, keyword argument, return, error, mutation and aliasing behavior, and must never be narrowed, deleted or refitted to this one signature. Semantics: int_repr returns the raw integer codes stored by an affine-quantized tensor (quint8 -> uint8, qint8 -> int8, qint32 -> int32) with the same shape as the input; the scale/zero-point metadata does not enter the result, so comparisons are exact (rtol=0, atol=0) and no autograd history is carried. Per-tensor quantization is covered unconditionally; per-channel (torch.per_channel_affine) coverage exists only where the backend declares float64 and int64 support, so it is capability-gated. Rank-0 and zero-sized quantized inputs are valid, and transpose / offset slice / strided slice / zero-stride expand / channels_last views read exactly like a compact clone. Overload-dependent behavior lives in the original tests: the .out overload takes a keyword-only `out` buffer, returns that same buffer (alias of the out parameter), resizes a too-small buffer, writes through a strided buffer, rejects a mismatched out dtype, and must not disturb the quantized input; a same-device out buffer is what the supplied rows use, and the source's native-backend note about requiring the out tensor on the input's device is not exercised by any test row. Non-quantized dtypes are asserted to fail with RuntimeError only on the CUDA/NVIDIA snapshot (the negative rows are built when vendor_name is "nvidia"); a non-tensor argument fails with RuntimeError/TypeError. Broadcasting and backward do not apply to this operator.
